Nigeria’s number two wheelchair player Wasiu Yusuf has hailed the ongoing Destiny Ford Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship as a major boost for the sport in Nigeria, following the introduction of wheelchair doubles and a veterans’ category. Yusuf said the N30m championship had given athletes with disabilities a platform to show their abilities while competing for significant prize money. he explained the wheelchair doubles event was particularly important because it had never featured in their competitions before. “I am happy that once again we have a championship where people with disabilities can showcase what they are made of. It is the best financial prize for able-bodied and wheelchair players,” he said. “We have never played wheelchair doubles before now, but at this championship we have wheelchair doubles and veterans’ events. We are grateful for this because it has changed the face of wheelchair tennis in Nigeria.” The nine-day championship, organised by the Destiny Ford Da-Silva Foundation, began on Friday at the tennis section of the National Stadium, Surulere, Lagos, and runs until November 21. The men’s and women’s singles champions will each receive N1.5m, while the remaining prize money will be shared among the other categories. Organisers have also provided a ₦30,000 subsidy for every main-draw player. Da-Silva, a former Nigerian number one and Davis Cup star, said the event was his way of giving back to the sport that shaped his career. He recalled the Governor’s Cup Lagos Tennis Championship, which was held when Tinubu was Lagos governor, and said younger players deserved similar opportunities. The Governor’s Cup was rebranded as the Lagos Open in 2018. “I want to give back to tennis what tennis gave me. We used to have the Governor’s Cup Lagos Tennis Championship when President Bola Tinubu was Lagos governor. Unfortunately, that era is gone, and it is one of the reasons I felt that if I could enjoy that kind of benefit back then, the new generation of players deserved the same thing,” he said. “With the little God blessed me with, I decided to do something like that. It is a dream come true. If you come to the stadium, what you see is amazing because we have to give back to tennis.” Peter Akinbo Peter, who has been covering sports for PUNCH for close to two years, focuses on combat sports reporting, special features and human angle stories
